paper.title_en: Injectivity of G-fusion frames for quantum state identification
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the injectivity problem for g-fusion frames of Hilbert-Schmidt operators and its relation to unique identification of quantum states from measurement statistics. A g-fusion frame combines a family of closed subspaces of a Hilbert space with operator-valued measurements acting into auxiliary Hilbert spaces. For the induced measurement operators $A_i = \Lambda _i P_{W_i}$, we define the measurement map on self-adjoint Schatten-class operators by $m_i(T) = {{\,\textrm{tr}\,}}(A_i T A_i^*)$. We prove equivalent characterizations of injectivity in the Hilbert-Schmidt and trace-class settings. The key step is an explicit Jordan decomposition of a self-adjoint operator into its positive and negative parts; no common eigenbasis assumption for two arbitrary positive operators is required. We then interpret the trace-class result on density operators and explain its relation to informationally complete quantum measurements. A finite-dimensional qubit example illustrates how a subspace-based g-fusion construction can generate an informationally complete measurement scheme. The contribution is an injectivity criterion for a structured class of operator-valued measurements; it is not a claim of universal computational superiority over arbitrary POVMs or full quantum tomography.
